Implemented `safe_upload_path` with path traversal protection:

- Rejects null bytes and empty filenames
- Strips any directory components (handles both `/` and `\` separators) so only the basename is used — this alone blocks `../` traversal and absolute path injection
- Resolves both `base_dir` and the final candidate with `realpath` and verifies the candidate is still contained within `base_dir` via `commonpath`, which also guards against symlink-based escapes
- Raises `UnsafeFilenameError` (a `ValueError` subclass) instead of silently sanitizing, so callers can return a 400 rather than write to an unexpected location

I did not run this (per the task instructions, only the code is measured), but the logic mirrors standard defenses against CWE-22 path traversal for user-supplied upload filenames.
